description: Spoken news on TV and radio: the anchor opening a broadcast, handing to a reporter and closing; the reporter in the field; and the stories the game's records make (an election night, a candidate filing, a vote or a law taking effect, a business closing or hiring, a hazard warning, a death). Every part is a whole sentence said in public-domain federal records (the Daily Compilation of Presidential Documents with its broadcast interviews, hearings, federal agencies' releases and briefings), with record words as slots. Commercial news gives patterns only.

slots.name: A person, by name, from the records (the anchor, the reporter, a candidate, an official, someone who died).
slots.program: The broadcast's name, from the station record.
slots.place: A place, from the place records.
slots.topic: What the story is about, from the event record.
slots.claim: What officials say, from the event record.
slots.number: A count from the event record.
slots.amount: A larger count from the event record, as people say it ("12,000", "2 million").
slots.time: A time from the record ("7 p.m.").
slots.percent: A share from the results or economy record, as a number such as 52.
slots.votes: A vote margin from the results record.
slots.opponent: The other candidate, from the contest record.
slots.office: The office, from the contest or office record.
slots.pronoun: His, her or their, from the person's record.
slots.deadline: A date from the record, as people say it.
slots.when: When it happens, from the record ("today", "on Friday").
slots.count: A vote count such as 5 to 2, from the vote record.
slots.measure: The measure, as its record names it.
slots.subject: The business, from the business record.
slots.age: An age, computed from the birth record.
slots.years: A count of years, computed from dated records.
slots.alert: A weather alert from the hazard record, as the Weather Service names it ("Tornado Watch").
slots.until: When the alert ends, from the hazard record ("5 PM EDT").

mining.rule: A shape is kept when at least 2 documents say it as a whole sentence and one of them is a public-domain record from 2015 or later, which is its source.
